findings.title: Budget can be removed by the search loosening, contradicting the shopper's limit precedence
findings.problem: The tool schema allows the budget to be raised 25% or removed during loosening, while the system prompt makes a stated budget a limit that holds unless the shopper waves it aside.
findings.proof: claims, materials, products with no stated age, brand, category, the budget raised by 25%, the budget removed
findings.fix: State in the system prompt's Search rule that the budget is never loosened by the catalog tool, or remove the budget steps from the schema's loosening order, so the two sources agree.

findings.title: Router sentence is convoluted
findings.problem: The Router's buried-request rule is a long nested sentence that is hard to act on, which weakens the clarity of the routing step.
findings.proof: A message it would answer with fixed sentences alone is read once more by a model for a buried product request
findings.fix: Rewrite as two short sentences: if fixed sentences alone would answer the message, a second model pass checks it for a buried product request, and any such request is screened, routed and answered.

findings.title: No rule for children's personal data
findings.problem: The context has no rule for data about children, even though products are often bought for under-13s and the screen only removes e-mail, phone, card and ID patterns.
findings.fix: Add to the Personal details section an explicit rule that the agent never asks for or stores a child's name, age-linked identifiers or school, and that such details are dropped before any model sees them.

findings.title: Catalog products carry no recall check
findings.problem: Recall checks are required only for products looked up on the web, so a catalog product is never checked for recall and the context does not say so to the shopper.
findings.fix: Add a rule that catalog-only products are marked as not checked for recalls and that the reply says so, or require a web recall check for each recommended product.

findings.title: Input screen detection method is unspecified
findings.problem: The input screen removes instruction-like clauses, but the context does not say whether this is pattern matching, a classifier or a model, so its coverage cannot be checked.
findings.proof: A clause that tries to change the instructions, asks for prompts or keys, dictates the reply's wording or asks which chemicals to mix is removed
findings.fix: Name the detection method and list its test cases, or add a sentence that the screen is code-based and tested against a set of injection examples in the release tests.

findings.title: rag.search description is overlong and partly duplicates the policy
findings.problem: The rag.search description runs to several hundred words, including routing and loosening rules that the system prompt already covers, which costs tokens on every call.
findings.proof: Not for a current price, stock or a customer rating: the catalog has none of these (web.search does).
findings.fix: Shorten the description to when to call, the filter semantics and the result fields, and leave the loosening and safety rules to the system prompt.

findings.title: Loosening rule is repeated in the system prompt
findings.problem: The system prompt restates the catalog tool's never-loosened rules, which the tool schema already gives in full.
findings.proof: never a stated age range or a safety exclusion
findings.fix: Keep one statement of the loosening rules, in the system prompt or the schema, and refer to it from the other.

findings.title: Catalog size facts repeated across files
findings.problem: The catalog's size and snapshot date appear in the knowledge file and again in the tool description, adding tokens without new information.
findings.proof: Amazon Product Dataset 2020, cleaned: 9,740 products from 2,204 brands, one snapshot from January 2020.
findings.fix: Keep the size and snapshot facts in one place, preferably the knowledge file, and cut the copy in the tool description.

findings.title: Column name Ingredients does not match its content
findings.problem: The table column is called Ingredients but holds materials and claims, which can lead the model to report ingredients a listing never states.
findings.fix: Rename the column to Materials & claims in the goal and in the table spec.

metadata.role: voice shopping assistant for product discovery (recommends and compares products; it cannot buy, change or access anything)
metadata.business_case: A shopper speaks or types a request. It has no accounts, no orders, no payments and no personal records; both tools are read-only.
metadata.goal: Recommend up to three products that fit what the shopper asked for, state only what the retrieved evidence states, cite a source for every product, keep the spoken reply short, refuse unsafe requests, and stay within product discovery.
